items.definition:
enjoyment or vigor in doing something
He tackled the project with great gusto.

an attacking player in certain team sports, such as football or rugby
The halfback ran the ball down the field.

a person of the counterculture of the 1960s
My aunt was a hippy in her youth.

the habit or principle of being independent and self-reliant
The culture emphasized individualism and personal freedom.

a speech impediment in which s and z are pronounced like th
The child had a slight lisp when he spoke.

a large, destructive grasshopper that forms swarms
A swarm of locusts destroyed the crops.

an unlucky accident
A minor mishap delayed the flight.

a thick, dark syrup
She used molasses to sweeten the gingerbread.

a dramatic entertainment, originating in ancient Rome, in which performers express meaning through gestures accompanied by music
The children enjoyed the clown's pantomime.

an object or surface that reflects light, sound, or heat
The cyclist had a reflector on the back of his bike for safety.

a place where birds regularly settle or congregate to rest at night
The chickens returned to their roost at dusk.

a utensil consisting of a wire or plastic mesh held in a frame, used for straining solids from liquids or for separating finer from coarser particles
She used a sieve to drain the pasta.

a shelf or slab of stone, wood, or metal at the foot of a window or doorway
She placed the potted plant on the window sill.

a marine fish of warm seas, valued as food
We caught a large red snapper on our fishing trip.

a suppressed, typically scornful laugh
I heard a snicker from the back of the room.

a person who performs a solo
The violinist was the soloist for the concert.

a person from the south of a country or region
She is a proud Southerner, born and raised in Georgia.

A blade or plate that rotates or moves in response to a fluid flow.
The weather vane on the roof showed the direction of the wind.

And other similar things; a small piece of furniture with shelves.
We bought some snacks, drinks, and whatnot for the party.

A person who accuses someone.
The accuser presented strong evidence against the defendant.

a charm or ornament worn to protect against evil
She wore an amulet around her neck for good luck.

a note added by way of comment or explanation
The student added several annotations to the text.

a member of the aristocracy
The aristocrat lived in a grand mansion.

a type of tropical seabird
The blue-footed booby is known for its distinctive feet.

the activity or occupation of keeping records of the financial affairs of a business
Good bookkeeping is essential for any small business.

a member of a French-speaking population in Louisiana
Cajun cuisine is famous for its spicy flavors.

the place where Jesus was crucified
The sermon spoke of the suffering at Calvary.

a large barrel-like container made of wood, used for liquids
The wine was aged in an oak cask.

a narrow walkway, especially one high up in a building or used by models
The models walked down the catwalk showcasing the new collection.

compulsory enlistment for state service, typically into the armed forces
Many countries have abolished military conscription.

the notional environment in which communication over computer networks occurs
Hackers operate in cyberspace, often across national borders.

a priest, magician, or soothsayer in the ancient Celtic religion
Ancient Celtic societies were led by powerful druids.

a thing that fails to work or is unsatisfactory
The fireworks were a dud; none of them lit up.

a person who ensures that rules or laws are obeyed
The police act as enforcers of the law.

a silly or foolish person; a mistake
I made a goof on the exam and lost points.

the cry of an owl; something very amusing
The comedian's jokes were a real hoot.

a person who gives information to the police or other authority, especially against criminals
The police received a tip-off from an anonymous informer.

A former monetary unit of Italy, Turkey, and other countries.
Before the euro, Italy used the lira.

A large diving waterbird, or a foolish/crazy person.
The loon's call echoed across the lake.

A large, high-speed computer, especially one used by an organization for complex operations.
Many large corporations still rely on mainframes for their core operations.

A grinding tooth at the back of a mammal's mouth.
The dentist said I had a cavity in my back molar.

the process of bringing something back to a normal state
The normalization of relations between the two countries took years.

a burden or responsibility
The onus is on the prosecution to prove guilt.

a type of chalcedony with parallel bands of different colors
She wore a beautiful necklace with a black onyx pendant.

a synthetic fiber made from regenerated cellulose
This dress is made of soft rayon fabric.

the quality or state of being rigid or stiff
The rigidity of the metal made it difficult to bend.

a type of dark, reddish-brown wood
The antique cabinet was crafted from beautiful rosewood.

a type of dog; a person who sets something
The English Setter is a popular breed for hunting.

a small, thin, pointed piece that has been broken, cut, or torn off something
He got a tiny sliver of wood stuck under his fingernail.

a flexible board used for jumping; a source of ideas or actions
His first successful startup served as a springboard for his future ventures.

food and drink regarded as a source of strength; the maintaining of someone or something in existence
The hikers carried enough sustenance to last them for several days.

a device allowing a part to turn freely on a pivot
The office chair has a swivel base, allowing it to rotate easily.

a man who practices witchcraft; a sorcerer
The warlock cast a powerful spell.

the edge of a road or path
Many good ideas fall by the wayside if they are not properly developed.

a person or company that sells goods in large quantities at low prices to retailers
We buy our products directly from the wholesaler.

a medium for transmitting radio or television signals
The news was broadcast over the airwaves.

an independent person or body officially appointed to settle a dispute
They agreed to appoint an independent arbitrator to resolve the conflict.

an angel of the highest rank
The archangel Gabriel delivered the message.

a male singing voice between tenor and bass
He has a rich baritone voice.

lineage; ancestry
The royal bloodline was carefully preserved.

frontier region; border area
Life in the borderland can be challenging.

the position or rank of a captain
His captaincy of the team was a great success.

the position or period of being a chairman
Her chairmanship of the committee lasted five years.

a variety of white wine grape; a dry white wine
We ordered a bottle of crisp Chardonnay with dinner.
